# n9 - The four blockers the post-execution review found

v1's reviewer dogfooded the runner end to end against a real scratch repository and found four ways
the gate does not hold. Two of them mean the runner cannot work at all, and two mean it writes
`done` on work nothing verified. The whole review lives at
`resources/review--post-execution-2026-09-11.md`; read it before touching anything.

The first is the one that matters most. `RunnerAbsorb.absorb` reads the return's schema and then
never reads the return's own `status:` again. An executor that says `needs_decision` with a
question, or `blocked` with a reason, has that answer discarded and its node written `done`. The
six mechanical checks were never meant to replace the executor's own verdict; they were meant to
sit behind it.

The second is the one that makes the rest academic. `RunnerCore.context` sets `plastic_home` from
`Arm.home_for`, which returns the parent of `.plastic`, so `CoreIntegrity` looks for
`manifest.json` in the operating-system home and never finds it. Every return is written `blocked`,
and `blocked` is not a state `runner answer` or `ReadySet` can release, so the node is stuck
without a hand edit to the ledger.

The third is a fail-open. `NodeWorktree.changed_paths` returns an empty array both when the diff is
empty and when git could not run, and a verify node has no branch to diff, so the diff-scope rule
that governs verify nodes has never once fired. The fix is to distinguish "no diff" from "could not
measure" and to refuse on the second.

The fourth is a lock hole. The absorb loop runs before the runner's only lock check, so a session
that does not hold `delivery.lock` writes transitions anyway, attributes them to the rightful
holder, and on the `done` path deletes a node worktree out from under a live executor.

## n9 failure-mode matrix
| Row | Operation | Failure mode | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 9.1 | Branch on the return's `status:` before the mechanical checks (B1) | A return saying `needs_decision` is written `done`, every downstream node unblocks on unfinished work, and the question vanishes, which is exactly what shipped | `runner_absorb_test#test_needs_decision_return_writes_needs_decision` |
| 9.2 | Carry the return's `question:` onto the `needs_decision` line (B1) | The node parks with no record of what was asked, so nobody can answer it | `runner_absorb_test#test_needs_decision_line_carries_the_question` |
| 9.3 | Write `blocked` and `failed_verification` from a return that says so, with its `reason:` (B1) | An executor that reports its own failure is recorded as a success | `runner_absorb_test#test_self_reported_failure_writes_its_own_state_and_reason` |
| 9.4 | Run checks 3 to 6 only when the return says `done` (B1) | A non-`done` return still pays for a merge and a full suite before being overwritten as `done` | `runner_absorb_test#test_mechanical_checks_run_only_for_a_done_return` |
| 9.5 | Resolve `context.plastic_home` to the `.plastic` directory, not its parent (B2) | `CoreIntegrity` looks for `manifest.json` in the operating-system home, no return ever reaches `done`, and every node lands in a `blocked` state nothing can release | `runner_cli_test#test_context_plastic_home_points_at_the_dot_plastic_dir` |
| 9.6 | Resolve `RunnerProposals`' template directory under the same corrected home (B2) | Scaffolding a proposed node reads `$HOME/templates` and finds nothing | `runner_absorb_test#test_proposals_template_dir_resolves_under_dot_plastic` |
| 9.7 | Reach the integrity check successfully against a real installed manifest (B2) | The fix is asserted only against a fixture and the real path stays broken | `runner_cli_test#test_core_integrity_finds_the_installed_manifest` |
| 9.8 | Return nil, not `[]`, from `NodeWorktree.changed_paths` when the diff cannot be computed (B3) | An unmeasurable diff reads as a clean diff and the scope gate passes on anything | `node_worktree_test#test_changed_paths_returns_nil_when_it_cannot_measure` |
| 9.9 | Measure a verify or research node's diff against the intent worktree, where it can actually make one (B3) | A verify node's branch never exists, so the diff always fails and D9's "any diff fails" has never once fired | `node_worktree_test#test_verify_node_diff_is_measured_against_the_intent_worktree` |
| 9.10 | Refuse a non-work node that produced any diff (B3) | A reviewer edits the code it is reviewing and the runner writes `done`, which is exactly what shipped | `runner_absorb_test#test_verify_node_with_a_diff_fails_scope` |
| 9.11 | Treat an unmeasurable diff as `failed_verification reason=scope_unmeasurable` (B3) | The fail-open survives the fix because nil is read as empty somewhere downstream | `runner_absorb_test#test_unmeasurable_diff_fails_verification` |
| 9.12 | Check the delivery lock in `run_step` before the absorb loop, not only in dispatch (B4) | A session that holds no lock writes transitions anyway, attributes them to the rightful holder, and deletes a live executor's worktree | `runner_cli_test#test_step_without_the_lock_writes_no_ledger_line` |
| 9.13 | Leave the ledger byte-identical when the lock check refuses (B4) | The refusal message prints and the write happens anyway, which is exactly what shipped | `runner_cli_test#test_refused_step_leaves_the_ledger_unchanged` |
| 9.14 | Block, not pass, when the project's verify command cannot be read because its record is malformed (M1) | A `project.yml` that fails to parse is indistinguishable from a project with no verify command, and `done` is written with `suite:absent` | `runner_absorb_test#test_unparsable_project_record_blocks_with_verify_command_unreadable` |
| 9.15 | Record `merge` in `gates=` only when a merge actually ran (M2) | The evidence field on the one line that matters claims a check that the code skipped for this kind | `runner_absorb_test#test_gates_records_merge_only_for_a_work_node` |

## Steps
1. Red: the matrix's tests above, committed before any code.
2. Fix the four blockers and the two majors, smallest change each.
3. Green, then the whole suite at its baseline.
